subject: Escrowed tranche schedule and smoothing for 3-year prepay
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@veridianhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Veridian Health Procurement <procurement@veridianhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Proposal — escrowed tranche schedule for 3yr prepay

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we discussed with procurement, Veridian is evaluating a 3-year prepay commitment to cover inference usage across our clinical analytics workload. We like Redwood's performance profile, but procurement wants a drawdown structure that avoids large up-front unrecoverable buckets while preserving term discounts.

Attached is a first-pass term sheet (20261105_Veridian_term_sheet_v1.pdf) with the commercial ask: 3-year commitment, $2.0M total prepay, and an effective blended discount target in the mid-teens. Procurement is specifically asking for an escrowed-tranche release mechanism that:
- Releases funds to Redwood on a monthly or quarterly cadence tied to consumption reporting (they prefer quarterly releases but will consider monthly with reconciliation)
- Includes a smoothing mechanism so high initial ramp doesn't consume more than X% of the first-year tranche
- Provides a make-whole if usage materially exceeds committed cadence in early months (so Redwood isn't starved)

Questions for you:
1) Can Redwood support an escrowed wallet with monthly reporting + quarterly releases?
2) What discount bands do you apply by annualized committed spend vs actual drawdown cadence?
3) Any recommended ramp schedule you typically see for customers with large seasonality (e.g., 3-6 month onboarding spike)?

Procurement wants a redline-ready term sheet within two weeks. Would appreciate a quick sketch of a feasible tranche schedule and any constraints from finance/recognition. Happy to jump on a quick call.

Best,
Ethan Cole
Head of IT Procurement
Veridian Health

Attachments: 20261105_Veridian_term_sheet_v1.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal — escrowed tranche schedule for 3yr prepay

Ethan — thanks for the detailed note and the term sheet. I copied Ben (sales ops) and Lauren (finance) so we can give you a commercially executable option quickly. Quick answers up front:

- Yes, we can support an escrowed wallet with monthly reporting and quarterly tranche releases. We can also do monthly releases with a 30–90 day reconciliation window if Veridian prefers cash cadence tied to usage.
- Discounting is tiered by committed ARR and exposure profile; for a $2M 3-year commit we can get into the low-to-mid teens depending on ramp protections and refundability.
- Typical smoothing: hold back 10–25% of year-1 funds in an escrow cushion that releases gradually over months 3–12, with an early-burn protection to cover spikes during onboarding.

Ben / Lauren — can you sketch two options: 1) quarterly release cadence with 20% year-1 holdback and 2) monthly release cadence with 15% holdback + monthly true-up? Please include accounting/recognition implications and what we can offer as a non-refundable vs refundable tranche.

Ethan — I can do a 30-minute call tomorrow (Nov 6) or Friday to walk through the options. Which works best for you?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

- Sales ops (Ben): confirm whether we can provide an option with quarterly releases (larger tranches) and a smaller discount bump to the customer, vs monthly releases with tighter reconciliation.
- Legal/Refundability: want to avoid open refund liabilities; propose refundable only for customer termination for convenience with pro-rata refund less migration fees. For customer default we retain balance.

I attached a draft escrow schedule spreadsheet (escrow_schedule_tab.xlsx) — please edit with numbers for the $2M example and two cadence options.

Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping in your team. A few clarifications from procurement after reviewing your staging suggestion:

- Quarterly releases look preferable from our cash ops perspective, but procurement will accept monthly releases if you can provide a simple monthly statement and a 30-day true-up.
- We are open to a holdback/cushion, but procurement will request a cap on the holdback (no more than 20% of year-1) and an explicit schedule for release tied to consumption tiers.
- On refundability: Veridian prefers refundable-held funds in case of prolonged platform outage >90 days or material SLA misses. We can accept non-refundable treatment for normal churn.
- Ramp: we want a 6-month ramp to 80% of committed run-rate, with a defined onboarding spike allowance (first 60 days up to 150% of pro-rata) before true-ups kick in.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to: monthly statements + 30-day true-up, holdback capped at 20% Y1, an SLA-based refundable clause for outages >90 days, and a 6-month ramp to 80%? If yes, procurement will request a redline to the attached term sheet with those items and ask for a final commercial by Nov 18.

Best,
Ethan
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Proposal — escrowed tranche schedule for 3yr prepay (next steps)

Ethan — appreciate the clarity. We can commit to the following commercial guardrails for a $2.0M, 3-year prepay negotiation:

1) Release cadence: monthly statement + 30-day true-up with option for quarterly releases if Veridian prefers (we will model both).
2) Holdback: capped at 20% of year-1 funds as an escrow cushion; schedule will be month-by-month release tied to consumption tiers.
3) Ramp protection: we accept a 6-month ramp to 80% of committed run-rate with an onboarding spike allowance (first 60 days up to 150% of pro-rata before true-ups apply).
4) SLA refund carve: refundable escrow for material platform outage >90 consecutive days (definition and measurement period to be clarified in the SOW).
5) Discounting: with the above protections we can offer a blended 15% discount on the $2.0M prepay (net of usage reconciliation). If Veridian elects quarterly releases instead of monthly true-ups, we can increase the discount to 16.5%.

Next steps: Ben will prepare two redlines (monthly release + monthly true-up; quarterly release cadence) and Lauren will add the accounting/revenue recognition notes for each. We will share a redline package and an updated escrow schedule by COB Nov 12. Please confirm preferred cadence and coordinate a 30-minute sync (I have availability Nov 9 at 10:00am PT or Nov 10 at 2:00pm PT).

Action items:
- Veridian: confirm preferred release cadence (monthly or quarterly) and accept the capped 20% holdback.
- Redwood (Ben): draft redline options and updated escrow_schedule_tab.xlsx for $2M example.
- Redwood (Lauren): accounting commentary for recognition and suggested SOW language for SLA refundability.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.
